title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page opens a new section: before exploiting the principles derived so far (presumably the combinatorics of Teichmüller groupoids and their symmetries, cf. the icosahedral/dodecahedral counts on pp. 61 and 63), Grothendieck says he must first develop the formalism of 'points base à l'infini' (base points at infinity).

He states the scope in a parenthetical NB.
- The starting point is dimension 1.
- Later one must return to the analogous phenomena in arbitrary dimension, attached to a divisor with normal crossings.

The setup is as follows.
- X is a regular local scheme of dimension 1, i.e. X = Spec A with A a discrete valuation ring (he may also impose a completeness or henselian condition; that line is illegible).
- x is the closed point and k = k(x) the residue field.
- (53) U = X \ {x} = {η} is the generic point, U = Spec K.
- (54) T_x = V(m_x/m_x^2) is the 'tangent space at x', a k-scheme. In EGA convention V(E) = Spec Sym(E), so T_x is the affine line of tangent vectors. Then T_x^* = T_x \ {0} is a G_m-torsor over k, non-canonically isomorphic to G_{m,k}.
- (55) The key claim is a canonical morphism of schematic (étale) fundamental groups π_1(T_x^*) → π_1(U).
- He notes that it is enough to treat the completion, because Û → U induces π_1(Û) → π_1(U).
- The page breaks off at 'd'ores on sait qu'on a ...'.

The intended mathematics, in modern terms: for K̂ = k((t)), with a uniformizer t identifying T_x^* with G_{m,k} = Spec k[t, t^{-1}], one has π_1^tame(G_{m,k}) ≅ Ẑ'(1) ⋊ Gal(k^s/k) ≅ Gal(K̂^tame/K̂). In residue characteristic 0 this is the full Gal(K̂) ≅ Ẑ(1) ⋊ Gal_k. Composing with the decomposition map Gal(K̂) → Gal(K) gives a homomorphism defined up to inner automorphism.

More precisely, a k-rational point of T_x^* (a rational tangent vector) gives a 'base point at infinity' of U. This is a fibre functor on finite étale U-schemes, via Puiseux/Kummer extensions of k((t)). It is canonical up to unique isomorphism along paths, and Galois-equivariant. These are exactly what are now called tangential base points.

The purpose is to define Galois actions on Teichmüller groupoids based at boundary (maximally degenerate) points of M_{g,ν}, e.g. at 0, 1, ∞ for P^1 minus three points.
errors: The morphism (55) is canonical only as an outer homomorphism, or as an honest map of fundamental groupoids once tangential base points are fixed. Without base points there is no canonical group homomorphism.

In residue characteristic p > 0, π_1(T_x^*) ≅ π_1(G_{m,k}) has a huge wild (Artin–Schreier) part that does not correspond to Gal(K̂). The clean identification only holds for the tame (or prime-to-p) quotients. The page does not yet restrict to the tame case; this may have been intended on the next lines.
Minor: the notation V(m/m^2) = V̌((m/m^2)^∨) is consistent with EGA conventions, so there is no error there. The transcription's '(m/m_x^2)' inside V̌ should read the dual (m_x/m_x^2)^∨ or similar.

ideas.what: Base points at infinity: the punctured tangent space T_x^* of a curve at a point x serves as a base point for π_1 of the generic point / punctured neighbourhood, with a canonical map π_1(T_x^*) → π_1(U).
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Deligne, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points' (1989), §15; also attributed to Grothendieck's 'points base à l'infini' (Longue Marche, Esquisse) by Ihara, Nakamura and others.
ideas.where_published: Probably discussed in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) and alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); not certain of exact passages.

ideas.what: Identification of the tame Galois group of a complete DVR fraction field with π_1^tame of the punctured tangent line, Ẑ'(1) ⋊ Gal_k.
ideas.modern_name: Structure of tame Galois group of local fields / Abhyankar's lemma

ideas.what: Programme to extend base points at infinity to arbitrary dimension relative to a normal crossings divisor, i.e. punctured normal bundles at intersection strata.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximally degenerate points / normal-crossing base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989); Nakamura, Ihara–Nakamura (1990s), on maximal degeneration points of M_{g,n}

missed.claim: This is an early, explicit, dated-to-the-Teichmüller-notes formulation of tangential base points as π_1 of the punctured tangent space mapping to π_1 of the generic point, from roughly 1978–81. It predates Deligne's 1989 published treatment and shows Grothendieck's independent formalism. Its existence is known through Esquisse and Longue Marche citations, so this is priority documentation rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: il me faut encore développer le formalisme des "points base à l'infini" ... T_x = V(m_x/m_x^2) ... morphisme canonique Π̂_1(T_x^*) → Π̂_1(U)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Useful for historical attribution of tangential base points. Nothing mathematically new to a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up tangential base points ('points base à l'infini') in dimension 1, with the intended generalisation to normal crossing divisors. The idea is well known and already attributed jointly to Grothendieck and Deligne. The page is cut off before any non-routine content.
transcription_corrections: 'développer la formalisme' should read 'développer le formalisme'.

The NB reads roughly: 'Le point de départ est la dimension 1, mais une bonne partie s'étend [?] ... il sera nécessaire de revenir par la suite sur les phénomènes analogues en dimension quelconque, relatifs à la donnée d'un diviseur à croisements normaux...'.
After '(i.e. le spectre d'un anneau de valuation discrète A)' there is an interlinear phrase, possibly 'complet' or 'hensélien', which the transcription omits.
Before (54) the text likely reads 'l'anneau résiduel ... point générique' / 'son point générique, et' rather than an omission.
Line before (55): '[il y a] alors un morphisme canonique'.
Line after (55): 'Ici on a convenu' or similar (struck), then '(puisque Û → U donne Π̂_1(Û) → Π̂_1(U))', where Û is the completion.
The word 'complété' appears in the struck/overwritten line.
